title: Notion for virtual event hosts on Mac: a guide to managing logistics
metaTitle: Notion for virtual event hosts on Mac: Organize Your Events
description: Learn how to use Notion for virtual event hosts on Mac to manage run of show documents, speaker briefings, and attendee coordination efficiently.
targetKeyword: notion for virtual event hosts on mac
intro: Notion for virtual event hosts on Mac provides a central hub for your run of show, speaker bios, and event logistics. You can use this platform to replace fragmented documents with a single, searchable workspace that works perfectly on your Mac.
tldr: Use Notion databases to track event speakers and session schedules.
Centralize run of show documents to avoid version control issues.
Use Lazur on your Mac to dictate notes or find specific event pages.
Connect your event registration data via CSV imports to track attendee lists.
Keep your workspace clean with clear page hierarchies and consistent tagging.

blocks.text: Start by creating a master database for your event sessions. Use the /database command to initialize a new table. Add properties for Date, Speaker, and Status. This allows you to view your schedule as a calendar or a list.

When you work on a Mac, you can use the Notion desktop app to keep your event pages open in separate windows. Press ⌘ + N to open a new window for a specific speaker briefing while keeping your main run of show visible.
Managing run of show with Notion

A run of show document needs to be precise. Use a table view for your schedule. Include columns for time, duration, and technical cues. You can drag and drop rows to adjust the schedule as speakers confirm their availability.

items: Create a template for speaker briefings to ensure consistency.
Use a status property to track if a speaker has submitted their slides.
Add a date property to every session for automated calendar views.
Create a separate database for vendor contacts and technical requirements.

blocks.text: Speeding up your workflow with Lazur

Lazur helps you stay focused while managing events. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about your current screen. You can ask Lazur to find a specific page or explain a complex Notion database filter. This keeps your hands on the keyboard and your eyes on your event data.

Use the dictation feature to draft speaker emails or internal notes. Hold the fn key and speak your thoughts directly into a Notion page. This is useful for capturing quick updates during live event rehearsals.

items: Overcomplicating the database structure with too many properties.
Failing to set clear permissions for team members viewing the event page.
Not testing your Notion links before the event goes live.
Ignoring the desktop app updates which may include performance fixes.

blocks.text: Event planning requires constant attention to detail. By moving your logistics into Notion, you reduce the time spent searching for files. Spend your time on the event itself, not on managing folders.

faq.question: Can I use Notion offline on my Mac?
faq.answer: Notion requires an internet connection to sync your pages. You can view cached pages if you have opened them previously, but edits may not sync until you are back online.

faq.question: How do I share my event schedule with speakers?
faq.answer: Click the Share button in the top right corner. You can invite guests via email or create a public link with read-only access.

faq.question: Is the Notion desktop app better than the browser?
faq.answer: The desktop app allows for better navigation with keyboard shortcuts and keeps your event workspace separate from your web browsing tabs.
